mainTopic: Whose opinion our משנה follows on liquids that flow out on שבת, the מוקצה disputes of רב and שמואל, and a new משנה on roasting and baking before שבת
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of whose opinion our משנה follows when it lets a person load an olive press or winepress right before שבת. רבי יוסי בר חנינא says it follows רבי ישמעאל. The אמורא רבי אלעזר says it follows the תנא רבי אלעזר, who permits honey and even olive and grape juice that flow out by themselves on שבת. The גמרא explains why each אמורא did not accept the other's source, and reports that רבי יוסי בר חנינא ruled like רבי ישמעאל in practice. Next comes a list of מוקצה cases: oil and mats of olive pressers, ship mats, and animals or dates set aside for purposes other than eating. In every case רב forbids and שמואל permits, following the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. Two short stories follow. In the first, a student who ruled like רבי שמעון in רב's town was placed in נידוי for disrespect. In the second, two students rescued items from a fire in different ways. Finally a new משנה begins: roasting and baking may start just before שבת only if the food reaches a basic stage before dark, with the קרבן פסח and the fire of the בית המוקד as exceptions.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: רבי עקיבא says he may not finish
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the ברייתא quoted earlier: רבי עקיבא rules that one may not finish crushing after dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי עקיבא says:] He may not finish.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the ברייתא that רבי יוסי בר חנינא brought on the previous amud. רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי ישמעאל and says you may not finish crushing once it gets dark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke about garlic, unripe grapes and grain stalks that were crushed before שבת. רבי ישמעאל says you may finish after dark, and that is why רבי יוסי בר חנינא said our משנה follows him. רבי עקיבא's opposing view is what you see here.

phrases.english: He may not finish.
phrases.notes: These are רבי עקיבא's words from the ברייתא quoted on the previous page.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא cited on the previous amud as רבי יוסי בר חנינא's source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: one may not finish crushing after dark.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: our משנה follows the תנא רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The אמורא רבי אלעזר offers a different source: our משנה follows the תנא רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: It is the opinion of רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer to 'whose view is our משנה?' He says it is the תנא רבי אלעזר. His source comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people here share a name. The אמורא רבי אלעזר is identifying the משנה with the much earlier תנא רבי אלעזר. This is an alternative to רבי יוסי בר חנינא's answer of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people named רבי אלעזר here. The one speaking is an אמורא. The one he quotes is a תנא from an earlier generation.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר the אמורא.

phrases.english: It is [the opinion of] Rabbi Elazar.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר the תנא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative source for the משנה, instead of רבי יוסי בר חנינא's רבי ישמעאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה follows the תנא רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: The source: honeycombs crushed before שבת
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about honeycombs crushed before שבת whose honey oozes out on שבת. The תנא קמא forbids it and רבי אלעזר permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Honeycombs that he crushed on ערב שבת, and the honey came out by itself, are forbidden. And רבי אלעזר permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that the תנא רבי אלעזר allows something that flows out by itself on שבת. That matches our משנה's permission to load the press.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The honey was crushed before שבת but only came out on שבת. The תנא קמא treats it as forbidden. רבי אלעזר says it is permitted because no action was done on שבת. That is the same idea as juice flowing from a press that was loaded before שבת.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: חַלּוֹת דְּבַשׁ שֶׁרִיסְּקָן בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
phrases.english: As we learned: honeycombs that he crushed on Shabbat eve
and [the honey] came out by itself — it is forbidden,
and Rabbi Elazar permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבי אלעזר's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה follows the תנא רבי אלעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of honeycombs, where רבי אלעזר permits honey that oozes out on שבת

steps.title: Why didn't רבי יוסי בר חנינא use רבי אלעזר's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי בר חנינא chose רבי ישמעאל rather than the תנא רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי בר חנינא — what is the reason he did not say like רבי אלעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי בר חנינא did not accept רבי אלעזר's source. It is setting up an explanation of the difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's source looks like a direct parallel, since a crushed item releases its contents on שבת. So the גמרא wants to know what objection רבי יוסי בר חנינא had to it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina —

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר?
phrases.english: what is the reason he did not say like Rabbi Elazar?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the first אמורא did not use this seemingly good source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוסי בר חנינא rejected the honeycomb source

steps.title: Honey stays food; olive juice turns into liquid
steps.stepSummary: Honey is food before and after it comes out. Olives and grapes start as food but release liquid, so the honey case may be more lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could tell you: There, it is food at the start and food at the end. Here, at the start it is food and now it is liquid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוסי בר חנינא. The honey case is different from our משנה, so it cannot be its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Honey counts as food both in the comb and outside of it, so nothing changes its status. Olives and grapes turn from food into a drink (משקה), which is what squeezing really is. רבי אלעזר may have permitted honey but not olive oil or wine.

phrases.english: He can say to you: it is there [in the honey case]
that at the start it is food and at the end it is food,
[but] here, at the start it is food and now it is liquid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ, הָתָם הוּא דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא אוֹכֶל וּלְבַסּוֹף אוֹכֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by distinguishing honey from olives and grapes.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Honey stays food, but olives and grapes become liquid. So רבי אלעזר's leniency may not extend to our משנה.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי אלעזר permits olives and grapes too
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers back with a ברייתא brought by רב הושעיא. In it, the תנא רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון permit even olives and grapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר could tell you: We have heard that רבי אלעזר permits even olives and grapes. For when רב הושעיא came from נהרדעא, he brought a ברייתא with him: Olives and grapes that he crushed on ערב שבת and the juice came out by itself are forbidden. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון permit.
steps.whatsHappening: The אמורא רבי אלעזר rejects the difference between honey and olives. He has a ברייתא where the תנא רבי אלעזר explicitly permits olive and grape juice too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The food-versus-liquid distinction only works if the תנא רבי אלעזר never addressed olives and grapes. רב הושעיא's ברייתא shows that he did, and that he permits them. So רבי אלעזר's source fits our משנה exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: We have heard (it known) of him

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar can say to you:
But we have heard of Rabbi Elazar
that he permits even olives and grapes as well.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא,
phrases.english: For when Rav Hoshaya came from Nehardea,
he came and brought a baraita in his hand:
Olives and grapes that he crushed from Shabbat eve
and [the liquids] came out by themselves — they are forbidden.
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר לָךְ: הָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the honey-versus-olives distinction from step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The distinction between food that stays food and food that becomes liquid
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An explicit ברייתא shows the תנא רבי אלעזר permits olive and grape juice too.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר חנינא didn't know the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי בר חנינא never heard רב הושעיא's ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי בר חנינא had not heard the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question simply. רבי יוסי בר חנינא did not know this ברייתא, so he relied on the honey-versus-olives distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This does not say רבי יוסי בר חנינא's reasoning was wrong in itself. He simply lacked a source that would have answered it. That is why he looked to רבי ישמעאל instead.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנאית teaching outside the משנה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina —
he had not heard the baraita.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא בָּרָיְיתָא לָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the tension created by the ברייתא in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Lack of knowledge of a source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי בר חנינא deliberately rejected רבי אלעזר's view even though it was proven to cover olives.
steps.terutzMaskana: He simply did not know the ברייתא.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי אלעזר use רבי ישמעאל as the source?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא asks the reverse question: why didn't רבי אלעזר say the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר — what is the reason he did not say like רבי יוסי בר חנינא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side. It asks why רבי אלעזר did not accept רבי ישמעאל as the source, setting up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל also permits finishing crushing after dark, so he seems to fit the משנה. The גמרא wants to know what rules him out for רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar — what is the reason

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא?
phrases.english: he did not say like Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the question of step 4, now aimed at רבי אלעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי אלעזר rejected רבי ישמעאל as the source

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל only permits items that already had basic crushing
steps.stepSummary: Based on רבי יוחנן, the dispute between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא applies only to items that still need fine grinding. Items lacking basic crushing are forbidden by everyone, and our משנה's olives are like that.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could tell you: Wasn't it said about this: רבא בר חנינא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Where they still lack basic crushing, everyone agrees [it is forbidden]. They disagree only where they still lack fine grinding. And these [olives and grapes in the press] are like items still lacking basic crushing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains that רבי ישמעאל's leniency is too narrow to cover our משנה. Even רבי ישמעאל forbids items that still need their main crushing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן limits the dispute to items that were already crushed and only need a final fine grinding. Olives and grapes loaded into a press have not yet had their main crushing. So even רבי ישמעאל would forbid them, and he cannot be the source for our permissive משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a later אמורא can narrow a תנאית dispute. Once רבי ישמעאל's case is narrowed, it no longer fits our משנה.

phrases.english: He can say to you: Was it not stated about it —

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rava bar Chanina said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
where they lack [basic] crushing —
everyone agrees [it is forbidden];
where they disagree is where they lack [fine] grinding.
And these, too, are comparable to items lacking crushing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by narrowing the dispute between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי ישמעאל permits only items that already had their basic crushing. Our משנה's olives have not, so he cannot be its source.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר חנינא ruled like רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: In practice, רבי יוסי בר חנינא ruled like רבי ישמעאל and allowed finishing after dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא ruled in accordance with רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a practical הוראה. רבי יוסי בר חנינא followed רבי ישמעאל and let someone finish the work after dark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that רבי יוסי בר חנינא's view was not only theoretical. He relied on it in practice, in line with the opinion he identified as the source of the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on whose opinion the משנה follows. רבי יוסי בר חנינא says רבי ישמעאל, and he ruled that way in practice. רבי אלעזר says the תנא רבי אלעזר, who permits even olive and grape juice. רבי יוחנן's teaching limits רבי ישמעאל's leniency to items that only lack fine grinding.

phrases.aramaic: הוֹרָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina ruled in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion with a practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, רבי יוסי בר חנינא ruled like רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: Olive pressers' oil and mats: רב forbids, שמואל permits
steps.stepSummary: A new topic, מוקצה. רב forbids moving the oil and mats of olive pressers on שבת, and שמואל permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Oil of the olive pressers and mats of the olive pressers: רב forbids and שמואל permits.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the olive press was mentioned, the גמרא moves to a related topic. Can the press workers' oil and mats be used or moved on שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: These items are set aside for work, so רב treats them as מוקצה. שמואל generally does not apply the מוקצה prohibition in such cases, so he permits them.

phrases.english: Oil of the olive pressers
and mats of the olive pressers —
Rav forbids and Shmuel permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל בַּדָּדִין וּמַחְצָלוֹת שֶׁל בַּדָּדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Associative jump from the olive press to מוקצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items of olive pressers: רב forbids (מוקצה), שמואל permits.

steps.title: Ship mats: the same dispute
steps.stepSummary: The same מחלוקת applies to mats used to cover goods on a ship. רב forbids and שמואל permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those mats of the ships: רב forbids and שמואל permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists another item set aside for work, with the same dispute between רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These mats are set aside for covering merchandise, so they are another case of something reserved for a purpose. The pattern stays the same: רב treats it as מוקצה and שמואל does not.

phrases.english: Those mats of the ships —
Rav forbids and Shmuel permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another example of the same dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ship mats: רב forbids, שמואל permits.

steps.title: Animals and dates set aside for other uses
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reports that animals kept for milk, wool, eggs or plowing, and dates kept for trade, are forbidden as food by רב and permitted by שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: A goat for its milk, a ewe for its wool, a hen for its eggs, plowing oxen, and dates for business — רב forbids, and שמואל says: permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן lists more cases of things set aside for a purpose other than eating. רב says they cannot be eaten (or slaughtered) on שבת or יום טוב, and שמואל allows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner did not plan to eat these before שבת began, so for רב they are מוקצה. שמואל holds that this kind of setting aside does not create a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: A goat kept for its milk

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
A goat for its milk, and a ewe for its shearing,
and a hen for its egg,
and plowing oxen, and dates for commerce —
Rav forbids, and Shmuel says: permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the same רב and שמואל dispute to food items set aside for other uses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items set aside from eating: רב forbids, שמואל permits.

steps.title: They follow the dispute of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב and שמואל are following the תנאים: רבי יהודה (who holds of מוקצה) and רבי שמעון (who does not).
steps.simpleTranslation: And they disagree in the dispute of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ties all these cases to one root. רב follows רבי יהודה and שמואל follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that setting something aside makes it מוקצה. רבי שמעון generally does not accept this kind of מוקצה. So the whole list of disputes comes down to one earlier מחלוקת between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside, so it may not be used or moved on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: In every case on this list, רב forbids and שמואל permits. רב follows רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה. שמואל follows רבי שמעון, who does not.

phrases.aramaic: וְקָמִיפַּלְגִי בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: And they disagree in the dispute of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָמִיפַּלְגִי בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the root of all the listed disputes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב follows רבי יהודה (מוקצה applies). שמואל follows רבי שמעון (no מוקצה).

steps.title: A student rules like רבי שמעון and is excommunicated
steps.stepSummary: A student ruled like רבי שמעון that מוקצה is permitted, in the town of חרתא דארגיז, and רב המנונא put him in נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a student who ruled in חרתא דארגיז like רבי שמעון, and רב המנונא excommunicated him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a student who publicly ruled like רבי שמעון, the lenient view on מוקצה. A senior rabbi, רב המנונא, punished him with נידוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that רב follows רבי יהודה (strict on מוקצה) and שמואל follows רבי שמעון (lenient). The student followed the lenient view, yet he was punished. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He ruled / taught a halachic decision

phrases.english: There was a certain student who ruled
in Ḥarta De'argiz in accordance with Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: He permitted מוקצה, following רבי שמעון's lenient view.

phrases.english: and Rav Hamnuna excommunicated him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life story about the רבי יהודה / רבי שמעון argument over מוקצה that was just explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student who ruled leniently like רבי שמעון in that town was placed in נידוי by רב המנונא.

steps.title: But don't we rule like רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the student was punished, since the accepted halacha follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't we hold like רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. If the halacha really follows רבי שמעון, the student ruled correctly, so why was he punished?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes the well-known rule that on מוקצה the halacha follows רבי שמעון, the lenient view. If so, the student's ruling was correct and the punishment looks unfair. The גמרא needs a reason that has nothing to do with whether the ruling was right.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold (this is our accepted view)

phrases.english: But don't we hold in accordance with Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the punishment described in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's decision to place the student in נידוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the halacha follows רבי שמעון, the student ruled correctly and should not have been punished.

steps.title: It was in רב's town, so it was disrespectful
steps.stepSummary: The town was under רב's authority, and the student should not have publicly ruled against רב there.
steps.simpleTranslation: It happened in רב's place, and he should not have done this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the problem was not the content of the ruling but where it was given. Ruling against רב in a town under רב's authority was disrespectful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a correct, lenient ruling should not be issued publicly against the local rabbi's view in his own area. The נידוי was a punishment for disrespect toward רב, not for a wrong ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: In רב's place (where רב was the local authority)

steps.whatToRemember: We do rule like רבי שמעון on מוקצה. Still, one may not publicly rule against a רב in the town under his authority.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is NOT saying the student's ruling was wrong. The ruling itself was fine. The problem was ruling against רב in רב's own town.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story is a source for the principle of respecting the local rabbi's authority (מרא דאתרא).

phrases.english: It was in the place of Rav,
and he should not have done this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the reason for the punishment: it was about respect for authority, not about the halacha itself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The נידוי showed that the ruling like רבי שמעון was wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling was correct, but issuing it in רב's town was disrespectful to רב.

steps.title: Two students rescue items from a fire in different ways
steps.stepSummary: One student rescued items from a fire one vessel at a time, and another carried four or five vessels at once. Their difference matches the argument between רבה בר זבדא and רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were two students. One would rescue with one vessel, and one would rescue with four or five vessels. They argue in the same disagreement as רבה בר זבדא and רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second short story about two students, who rescued belongings from a fire on שבת in two different ways. It then points out that their difference is the same as an argument found elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rescuing some items from a fire on שבת is allowed within certain limits. The question is whether it is better to carry one vessel at a time or several at once. The גמרא does not decide here. It only links the students' behavior to the known argument between רבה בר זבדא and רב הונא, which is discussed elsewhere in the מסכת.

phrases.english: These two students:
one would rescue with one vessel,
and one would rescue with four and five vessels,
and they disagree in the dispute
of Rabba bar Zavda and Rav Huna.
phrases.notes: Their argument appears elsewhere in מסכת שבת, in the laws of rescuing items from a fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about students, mentioned in passing after the story of the student in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two students' different ways of rescuing items match the argument between רבה בר זבדא and רב הונא.

steps.title: New משנה: roasting food right before שבת
steps.stepSummary: Meat, onion or egg may be roasted before שבת only if there is enough time for them to roast while it is still day.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not roast meat, an onion or an egg unless there is enough time for them to be roasted while it is still day.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that you may put meat, onion or egg on the fire just before שבת only if they can reach a roasted state before nightfall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה allowed starting some processes before שבת that finish by themselves on שבת. Cooking food is stricter. Roasting must be done, or mostly done, before שבת begins. One reason is the worry that a person might stir the coals on שבת to speed up the cooking.

keyTerms.meaning: While it is still day (before שבת begins)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may not roast meat, an onion, or an egg
unless there is enough time for them to be roasted while it is still day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is no longer about מוקצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roasting before שבת is allowed only if the food can be roasted before nightfall.

steps.title: Bread and cakes need a crust before dark
steps.stepSummary: Bread in the oven, or a cake on coals, may be put in at nightfall only if its face will form a crust while it is still day.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not put bread into the oven at nightfall, or a cake on top of coals, unless there is enough time for its face to form a crust while it is still day.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same idea to baking. Bread or a cake may be put in only if it will form a crust before שבת starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With baking, the minimum stage is that the face of the bread forms a crust. Once it reaches that stage before nightfall, the rest of the baking may finish on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat cake baked on coals
That its face forms a crust

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נוֹתְנִין פַּת לַתַּנּוּר עִם חֲשֵׁכָה,
phrases.english: One may not place bread in the oven at nightfall,
nor a cake on top of coals,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּקְרְמוּ פָּנֶיהָ מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם.
phrases.english: unless there is enough time for its face to form a crust while it is still day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין נוֹתְנִין פַּת לַתַּנּוּר עִם חֲשֵׁכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving from roasting to baking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread or a cake may be put in before שבת only if its face will form a crust before nightfall.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: only the bottom must form a crust
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says it is enough if the bottom side of the bread forms a crust before nightfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: enough time for its bottom side to form a crust.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה. He sets a lower minimum for baking before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion needs the face of the bread to form a crust. רבי אליעזר needs only the bottom side, which takes less time. So his view allows putting the bread in later.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
enough time for its bottom side to form a crust.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing, more lenient opinion on the baking rule in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, it is enough if the bottom of the bread forms a crust before nightfall.

steps.title: Exceptions: the קרבן פסח and the fire in the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The קרבן פסח may be lowered into the oven at nightfall, and the fire in the בית המוקד may be lit right before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may lower the קרבן פסח into the oven at nightfall. And one may light the fire in the bonfire of the בית המוקד.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists two exceptions where you may start a fire-related process at nightfall, even though it will finish on שבת. Both involve the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the food must reach a basic stage of cooking before שבת. When ערב פסח falls on ערב שבת, the קרבן פסח may be lowered into the oven at nightfall and roast on שבת. Likewise, the fire in the בית המוקד, a chamber in the בית המקדש where the כהנים warmed themselves, may be lit just before שבת and spread on its own. The גמרא will explain why these cases are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Kindle the fire (get it to catch)
Chamber of the Hearth in the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: Food must normally reach a basic stage of cooking before שבת: roasted food must be roasted, and bread must form a crust (face, or only the bottom according to רבי אליעזר). The קרבן פסח and the בית המוקד fire are exceptions.
steps.confusionAlert: These exceptions do not mean the general rule is wrong. The rule still applies to ordinary cooking and baking. These are special cases connected to the בית המקדש.

phrases.aramaic: מְשַׁלְשְׁלִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח בַּתַּנּוּר עִם חֲשֵׁכָה.
phrases.english: One may lower the Paschal lamb into the oven at nightfall.
And one may kindle the fire
in the bonfire of the Chamber of the Hearth.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְשַׁלְשְׁלִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח בַּתַּנּוּר עִם חֲשֵׁכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives exceptions to the general rule of Steps 19–20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קרבן פסח may be lowered into the oven at nightfall, and the בית המוקד fire may be lit right before שבת.
